clue.text: Where to see Stanley wince endlessly when visiting Acton

indicators.note: one piece paying a visit goes inside the place named, so the trimmed word sits within the London district

parts.note: taken as written: Acton is a district of west London

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to wince is to cringe

explanation.surface: Someone at a game in a London suburb is grimacing at a player called Stanley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the synonym and 'when visiting' places it in Acton. Accrington Stanley is a Lancashire football club, so Stanley is a team, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrington Stanley is the football club based in the Lancashire town, so the town is where its team plays.

clue.text: Head leaves, disparages answers to crossword clues

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and it departs, so the synonym loses its opening letter

parts.note: to disparage someone is to slight them

explanation.surface: A boss walks out after belittling the solutions in a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: In crossword jargon each entry written in the grid is called a light.

clue.text: Desperate character kidnapping English churchman

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds a captive, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman character in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A frantic villain seizes an English clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the cow-pie-eating giant of the British children's comic The Dandy; 'kidnapping' puts E inside DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior cleric heading a cathedral chapter, so a churchman.

clue.text: Wicked Caliphs incarcerate Yankee corporal

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up, so the scrambled letters close round the extra letter
wicked suggests something twisted or bad, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Evil caliphs imprison an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' turns CALIPHS into PHSICAL, and 'incarcerate' puts Y inside it. 'corporal' looks like a soldier's rank but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal as an adjective means of the body, as in corporal punishment, which is the same as bodily.

clue.text: Experience uncharitable emotion when taking over from diplomat

indicators.note: taking one thing away from another removes it, with 'from' naming what loses the letter
completes 'taking ... from', marking the word that loses the letter

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent on a mission
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone feels resentment when succeeding a diplomat in post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking over from' reads as succeeding someone, but splits into 'taking ... from' as the removal signal and 'over' as O.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful longing for what another has, an unkind feeling, here as a verb.

clue.text: Boom created by this new electronic device

parts.note: a sonic boom is created on passing Mach one, written MACH I with the Roman numeral for one
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A new gadget is credited with causing a loud bang.
explanation.walkthrough: A sonic boom happens when an aircraft passes the speed of sound, Mach 1, written MACH I. 'electronic' looks like part of the definition but is E.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine is a mechanical or powered apparatus, so a device in the general sense.

clue.text: Like a latte? Kind Knut's round!

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, so the setter's possessive surrounds the word for kind

parts.note: Knut is the setter, so Knut's means the setter's, MY
ilk means kind or type

explanation.surface: The setter offers to buy the coffees: it is his round.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so Knut's means the setter's. 'round' looks like a round of drinks but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with a lot of steamed milk, so it is milky in colour and taste.

clue.text: Crew playing cards

definitions.meaning: ... are workers or crew members, as in all ... on deck
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

explanation.surface: Sailors pass the time with a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are both a ship's crew members and the sets of cards dealt to players.

clue.text: Sickly-looking sons touring each city in Wales

indicators.note: going on a tour round something encircles it, so the two letters go round the pale word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, so sons gives two of them
wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: Pale young men go travelling round a Welsh city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sons' supplies two S's, and 'touring' sends them round the word for pale rather than round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is the second-largest city of Wales, on its south coast.

clue.text: Obscure Britpop band

definitions.meaning: to make it indistinct, to obscure it
... were a leading 1990s British guitar-pop group

explanation.surface: A little-known group from the Britpop era.
explanation.definitionFit: Blur means to smudge or make unclear, and is also the name of the Damon Albarn group.

clue.text: Resort by North Sea where drinkers need to be upright

definitions.text: where drinkers need to be upright

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside town on the North Sea where the drinkers ought to be able to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a seaside town but is re-sort, the anagram signal for BY NORTH SEA. 'upright' means honest, not standing.
explanation.definitionFit: An honesty bar is unstaffed: guests take drinks and record them, trusted to pay, so they must be truthful.

clue.text: Terribly phony sibling's alternative therapy

indicators.note: done terribly, the word is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a sibling; the apostrophe-s is the possessive in the surface

explanation.surface: A sister's fake treatment is dismissed as fraudulent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' works on 'phony' alone; the possessive 's on 'sibling's' is just surface grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnosis is used as a complementary treatment for habits like smoking, outside mainstream medicine.

clue.text: Small hotel, eastern France, pocketing a bundle

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it away inside, so the letters enclose the single letter

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A little hotel in eastern France takes a wad of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts A inside SHEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, of corn stalks or of papers.

clue.text: Final word before one gets shot?

definitions.text: Final word before one gets shot?

parts.words: Final word before one gets shot?
parts.note: a photographer asks people to say this word to smile just before taking the picture, not before a firing squad

explanation.surface: Someone's last utterance before facing execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a firing squad, but it is a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask subjects to say cheese because the vowel makes them smile for the snapshot.

clue.text: Beccy (bless!) unwrapped cracknel — oddly a Lancs speciality

indicators.note: with the wrapping taken off, each word loses its outer letters
taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A girl called Beccy opens a sweet biscuit, a treat from Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapped' strips BECCY to ECC and BLESS to LES; 'oddly' picks CAKE from CRACKNEL. Lancs is Lancashire, the county of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a currant-filled pastry named after Eccles, a town historically in Lancashire.

clue.text: Simple fellow getting drunk outside

indicators.note: the drinker's word sits outside, wrapping round the abbreviation

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A naive man gets tipsy out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts SOT round F.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft is an informal British word for foolish or feeble-minded, as in soft in the head.

clue.text: Oscar and Roger (not Romeo in the end) covering New York's peak creative event

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece covers another by sitting above it

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed from the name
places the removed letter at the end of the name

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two friends from New York take over a high-profile arts festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ... in the end' drops the last R from ROGER, giving ROGE; in a down clue 'covering' puts O + ROGE above NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Orogeny is the geological process of mountain building, which literally makes peaks.

clue.text: That lady will shortly launch an attack

parts.note: she refers to that lady
will is shortened to 'll

explanation.surface: A woman is about to go on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE'LL, the contraction of she will, loses its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell is to bombard with artillery shells, a way of mounting an assault.

clue.text: Props up Marx reportedly propping up leaders of Soviet Union

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece props up another by sitting beneath it
the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.note: Marx said aloud is marks, and marks are stains

explanation.surface: Karl Marx's ideas are said to have supported the Soviet leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: MARX sounds like marks, meaning STAINS; 'propping up' places STAINS below SU in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to hold up or support the weight of something.

clue.text: Conservative Minister lacking some guts — he'll be moving sideways

indicators.note: the guts are a word's inner letters, and losing some of them removes one middle letter

parts.note: Dominic Raab was a Conservative government minister

explanation.surface: A spineless Tory cabinet minister keeps dodging the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: RAAB loses one of its middle A's. 'moving sideways' sounds like a political shuffle, but is how a crab walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs famously scuttle sideways across the shore.

clue.text: Indicates number of imperial units (about zero)

indicators.note: about means around, so the measures go around the round figure

parts.note: pints are units of volume in the imperial system
O resembles the figure zero

explanation.surface: Someone notes a quantity of pints, roughly nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PINTS round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To point is to show or signal, so points means shows the way.

clue.text: Father guarding old castles on a permanent basis

indicators.note: a guard stands round what it protects, so the title encloses the letter

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A priest keeps watch over ancient fortresses forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' puts O inside FR, giving FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: For keeps is an idiom meaning forever, permanently.

clue.text: One helps to observe sulphur being removed from resinous wine

indicators.note: the element's symbol is taken out of the wine's name

parts.note: retsina is a Greek wine flavoured with pine resin
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on taking sulphur out of Greek wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer of the eye, one of the parts that enable sight.

clue.text: Might wartime captive start to escape with support from Resistance?

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war might begin a breakout with help from the Resistance fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' reads as a modal verb, but it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Might as a noun is strength or force, which is power.

clue.text: Pet ate in RSPCA compound

indicators.note: in compound means mixed together, so the letters are combined in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An animal fed in an animal charity's enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an enclosure but is the anagram signal. The RSPCA is Britain's main animal welfare charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A Persian cat is a long-haired breed kept as a domestic companion animal.

clue.text: With which to clean top of orange juice cans

indicators.note: a can holds its contents, so the juice word contains the letter

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tip for scrubbing orange juice cans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cans' looks like a plural noun but is the verb: SAP holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is the everyday washing agent used to clean things.

clue.text: Battery where bird is served?

definitions.meaning: a single unit of an electric battery, and the word is used for a battery itself
bird is British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A battery farm, where poultry is dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British rhyming slang (birdlime, time) for a jail term, not a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is both a power unit and a prisoner's room in jail.

clue.text: Top of chimney pot caught bird of prey

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an owl is a nocturnal bird of prey

explanation.surface: A hawk was trapped on the top of a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a hood-shaped cover fitted on a chimney to improve the draught.

clue.text: Long story: ear needs boxing

indicators.note: the words box up the answer, which sits inside them across the gaps

explanation.surface: In a tall tale, someone's ear takes a clip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests a blow to the ear, but the words enclose the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something, to crave it, so the definition is the verb.

clue.text: Gary, Indiana football player missing taxi back

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the reversed vehicle is taken out of the player

parts.note: a linebacker is a defensive player in American football, as played in Indiana

indicators.note: backwards, so the vehicle's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A footballer from Gary, Indiana, has missed his ride home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAB into BAC, which 'missing' removes from LINEBACKER. Gary, Indiana is a US city, but Gary is the definition: Gary Lineker, England striker turned TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary Lineker is the former England striker and long-time presenter of the BBC football show Match of the Day.
